invariants: Every number the TAXBEN module uses comes from the rule book via ruleAsOf — no dollar, percent or month literals in the module (spec Tests; enforced by tests/taxben-rule-book-lint.test.ts)
A recorded capitalization decision is never rewritten by a later rule change or election change; the decision stores its reason and the rule value it used (TFA-1 late-change doctrine)
An unanswered business-use percent deducts 0% — never a guessed share (spec section 1)
Expensed (de minimis) units stay in the asset register and in the county snapshot; expensing is a tax treatment, not a removal (spec section 1, research: Weld DS 056)
The app prepares and estimates only — it never files a return; every benefit row states what the CPA must confirm (spec preamble)
Election-shaped defaults (de minimis on, bonus over Section 179) are starting values with DQ-TAXBEN questions filed for the CPA, never presented as owner answers
Money stays integer cents through existing functions; rule values that are dollars in the research convert once, at seed time

outcome: Every expense lands in the right deduction and the year's tax benefits are worked out automatically: each books expense account carries a deduction mapping (Schedule C line, percent, kind) with mixed-use business percentages asked once and 0% until answered; every purchase is expensed under the de minimis safe harbor or capitalized (bonus by default, Section 179 if the CPA prefers) with the plain-words reason recorded and expensed units kept in the asset register; a written capitalization policy is generated, signed on screen, stored as a business record and re-signed every December; costs from before the business began are tagged start-up and run through the Section 195 formula onto the Schedule C packet and the 4562 Part VI worksheet; and a Tax benefits page computes the year's benefit list — depreciation with a mid-quarter warning, vehicle mileage vs actual, home office both ways, QBI, self-employment rows, the retirement comparison, the enterprise-zone pre-certification To do, the county property value against the exemption, bad-debt and loss notes, and the ordinary-deductions checklist — every number read from the rule book and every row marked for CPA confirmation.
